items.title: A regular boundary disk attaches to a constant strip by actual Newton gluing
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use compact transverse strip data with generator $x$, boundary tori $L_0,L_1$, and a smooth path $J_t$. In one fixed chart about $x$ require $J_t=i$ for every $t$, $L_0=\mathbb R^m$ and $L_1=i\mathbb R^m$. Require $J_t=J_0$ for $0\le t\le\eta$ for some $\eta>0$. Let $v$ be an actual smooth nonconstant autonomous $J_0$-holomorphic closed disk with boundary on $L_0$ and marked boundary value $x$. Suppose its actual compact node-fixed linearization is onto of real index two.

For every sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$ there is an actual smooth finite-energy $J_t$ strip $g_\epsilon:x\to x$ obtained by attaching this disk at the lower boundary point $z=s+it=0$ of the constant strip $x$. More precisely use the disk half-plane coordinate $\zeta$ with marked point infinity, the node coordinate $w=-1/\zeta$, and fixed small cut radius $r$. Put
$$T=\pi^{-1}\log(r^2/\epsilon).$$
There is an explicit preglued map $u_T$, equal to $v(z/\epsilon)$ on the inserted disk core and to $x$ on the exterior strip, joined in the exact node chart. In actual boundary-preserving local-addition coordinates and the adapted cap/cylinder Sobolev norms of the sewn linear theorem, its correction obeys
$$\|\xi_T\|_{H^3}\le C(1+T)e^{-\pi T/2},\qquad g_\epsilon=\mathcal E(u_T,\xi_T).$$
It is the unique sufficiently small correction with the two fixed disk-core phases zero, on a ball of radius $c/(1+T)$. Its actual fixed-end linearization is onto of index two, with a right inverse of adapted norm at most $C(1+T)$, also in the actual unweighted $H^1\to L^2$ regularity sense. The corrected strips depend smoothly on positive $\epsilon$ locally away from zero.

As $\epsilon\downarrow0$ they converge smoothly to $x$ away from the attaching point and, in the source scaling $z=\epsilon\zeta$, smoothly locally to $v(\zeta)$ away from its node. Their energies converge to $E_g(v)$, with no lost energy. No kernel parametrization by translation and scale, nodal collar or exhaustion of all nearby strips is asserted.

items.title: Regular boundary disk caps have an actual nonlinear response graph
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix the actual regular node-fixed index-two boundary disk $v$, exact node frame and two compact-core phases in the cap response theorem. Use weight $0<\delta<\pi$ and choose its cut $\sigma=S$ sufficiently far into the exact node chart. Let
$$G_-^{5/2}=\{(g_n)_{n<0}:g_n\in\mathbb R^m,\ \sum_{n<0}(1+|n|)^5|g_n|^2<\infty\},$$
and define $G_+^{5/2}$ similarly.

For every sufficiently small pair $(g,c)\in G_-^{5/2}\times\mathbb R^m$ there is a unique actual $H^3$ map on the disk cap, near $v$, solving the autonomous holomorphic equation, with physical boundary on $L_0$, zero phases relative to $v$, and negative and constant modes of its difference from $v$ at the cut equal to $g$ and $c$. This is uniqueness in one fixed small cap neighborhood. Its positive-mode difference is a smooth response
$$\mathcal R(g,c)\in G_+^{5/2},\qquad \mathcal R(0,0)=0,$$
with bounded derivative and
$$d\mathcal R_{(0,0)}(g,c)=A_dg+B_dc$$
for the actual linear cap maps. The cap maps are smooth on their interior and up to the physical boundary away from the artificial cut; arbitrary higher smoothness of rough incoming data at that artificial cut is not asserted. Every actual nearby cap solution with the stated phase and trace data lies on this graph.

The graph is constructed from actual weighted Sobolev maps and their actual nonlinear section. It is not a formal graph or moduli axiom, and it supplies no neck matching or nodal exhaustion by itself.

items.title: Boundary disk attachment matching gives the actual scale and translation kernel
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the actual regular boundary-disk attachment data, phases and family $g_\epsilon$ of the Newton gluing theorem, with $T=\pi^{-1}\log(r^2/\epsilon)$. Choose the fixed cap cut sufficiently far in its exact chart. For all sufficiently large $T$, the nonlinear disk-cap response and the linear constant-strip-cap response match through the homogeneous neck in exactly one sufficiently small phase-fixed solution. It is precisely the Newton strip $g_\epsilon$.

The matched fixed disk-cap map differs from $v$ by $O(e^{-\pi T})$ in $H^3$; its derivatives with respect to $T$, of any fixed positive order in the fixed disk-core coordinates, are also $O(e^{-\pi T})$. The analogous assertions hold for the outer constant-strip cap. In particular, at every sufficiently small positive $\epsilon$ the actual fixed-end kernel is precisely
$$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\partial_s g_\epsilon,\ \partial_T g_\epsilon\}.$$
The two parameters given by longitudinal translation and $T$ smoothly parametrize the full local solution space at each such strip; after translation quotient, $T$ is a local coordinate.

Moreover any actual strip having these fixed cap neighborhoods, whose joining neck image lies in the exact chart and whose disk section has the prescribed zero phases, equals this matched strip for that fixed center and scale. This is actual uniqueness in those geometric neighborhoods. It does not yet prove that all strips converging to the nodal disk can be put into them with unique center and scale, or assert a globally injective nodal collar.

items.title: A regular boundary disk attachment has an exhaustive nodal half-collar
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the actual regular boundary-disk attachment data and the family $g_\epsilon$ with its fixed phases in the matching theorem. Consider the specified nodal configuration consisting of the constant strip $x$ and this one nonconstant disk $v$ at its lower boundary, with node value $x$ and no other bubble or strip component.

After applying the longitudinal normalization used in the convergence, every bounded-energy sequence of actual $J_t$ strips $u_n:x\to x$ converging to this configuration in the actual smooth component-core, complete energy and collapsed neck/tail sense of bubbled-strip compactness is eventually
$$u_n(s,t)=g_{\epsilon_n}(s-b_n,t),\qquad \epsilon_n\downarrow0$$
after a subsequence, with $b_n$ tending to its attaching position in the chosen longitudinal normalization. If only convergence, rather than monotone scales, is desired, the conclusion is $\epsilon_n\to0$ for the whole sufficiently late sequence with its chosen component normalization.

After decreasing $\epsilon_0>0$, two members with $0<\epsilon,\epsilon'<\epsilon_0$ are longitudinal translates only if $\epsilon=\epsilon'$ and that translate is the same center. The actual translation quotient therefore has a local nodal half-collar parametrized by $0\le\epsilon<\epsilon_0$, with zero the specified nodal disk orbit. Here the local topology is generated by the countable actual component-core, energy and neck/tail image tests described in the proof, and the ordinary actual solution topology at positive parameters. Thus this is a collar of actual solutions, with exactly one interval germ at this regular disk stratum.

The theorem presupposes an actual regular node-fixed index-two disk, not that all degenerations have that form. It supplies no low-index classification of other sphere/disk strata, no count for internal-pair components, and no target connected-sum or polygon gluing theorem.
